html:
On 4 November 1979, Iranian students supporting the Iranian Revolution stormed the United States embassy in Tehran and took its staff hostage. Fifty-two Americans were held for 444 days.

The students were angered that the deposed shah, Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, had been let into the US for cancer treatment, and remembered the 1953 coup. Khomeini backed them, and hardliners used the crisis to push out moderates. An American rescue mission failed in the desert in April 1980, and eight servicemen died.

The hostages were freed on 20 January 1981, minutes after Ronald Reagan took office, under a deal made in Algiers. The crisis helped end Jimmy Carter's presidency, and the United States and Iran have had no diplomatic relations since.
sum: On 4 November 1979, Iranian students supporting the Iranian Revolution stormed the United States embassy in Tehran and took its staff hostage. Fifty-two Americans were held for 444 days.
